title: Proposal: `%t` topic/tag/tab token

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

I just finished participating in [js13kgames.com](https://www.js13kgames.com/) and lemme tell you, debugging game loops are a pain, mainly because you cannot reasonably work with 10,000 logs a second: the inspector freezes before you can even make heads or tails of what you're looking at. And `debugger` obviously doesn't work, it halts the loop.

### What solutions exist today?

1. **Prefixing and filtering** - this doesn't prevent the thousands of logs from stalling out your inspector, though.
2. **Writing your own in-app debug panel** - we shouldn't have to do this, and it's particularly problematic in JS13k, it's hard enough as it is.

### How would you solve it?

I propose adding a native `%t` string substitution token to the standard formatting rules that map to a string or symbol:

```js
console.log("%tBall position: %f, %f", "physics", x, y);
console.log("%tDraw calls: %d", "render", drawCount);
```

This preserves the console's append-only nature while giving UAs a hook into features like console tabs that only have to render the logs of that topic.

As a bonus, you could log to multiple topics in the same call:

```js
console.log("%t %t Ball position: %f, %f", "physics", "render", x, y);
```

### Anything else?

This is in-part in remedy to `console.context()`'s snag. It allows for a unified, cross-environment "sublogger" without breaking console's existing model overall.
